Use for interactive Continual-ARC instances with a test grid, demonstration requests, and scored submissions.

## Protocol first

- On every turn, provide exactly one action JSON object on the last line: `{"action":"submit","grid":[...]}`, `{"action":"request_demos"}`, or `{"action":"finish"}`. Do not add prose or unrelated tool calls to puzzle turns.

Validated task variants map a panel to color 1 when it contains exactly two markers; otherwise map it to that panel's background color. Ignore divider cells during counts and output; panel dimensions may be established by intersecting full-width and full-height lines or by a single orientation of separators. Confirm the exact count-to-output mapping from demos before use. See `references/session-lessons.md` for accepted examples including 2x2 panels from a 23x9 and an 8x5 input.

4. When the rule is underdetermined, request a demo specifically to distinguish plausible hypotheses. Avoid a low-information demo if a confident rule is already established.

# ARC template stamping

Use this when a demo shows a distinctive compact colored object and many single-cell markers on a background, and the output repeats the object around each marker.

1. Identify the background, source template, and marker color by comparing demo input/output. The source template is usually a small rectangular pattern whose background-colored cells are transparent.
2. Determine the anchor cell of the template from the demonstration: commonly a central template cell maps onto each marker. Verify this using multiple markers, including edge markers.
3. For each marker in the test grid, copy the template's non-background cells with the same relative offsets, centered/aligned on the marker; replace the marker as part of the stamp. Preserve unrelated background and the original source object unless the demonstration shows otherwise.
4. If stamps overlap, infer precedence from the demo and apply consistently. Keep grid dimensions unchanged; clip only if edge behavior is demonstrated.
5. A related rule (validated in task-e6f5b2c7): when the seed is a compact shape of color C on background B, use the shape's full bounding box and its C-cell mask. Scan same-sized windows for the marker/background value at every mask position; if a demo confirms mask-only matching, non-mask cells may be arbitrary and must not be constrained. Recolor the matched mask cells with C, preserving all other cells and the original seed. Add a non-mask constraint only when the demo clearly establishes one. Verify on the demo before applying; do not confuse this with recoloring arbitrary long background runs.

Validated mask-only variant (task-e6f5b2c7): the 5-colored seed mask in its 5x4 bounding box had relative cells `{(0,2),(1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(3,0),(3,1),(4,2),(4,3)}` (0-indexed). The 25x13 test likewise had exactly two such placements, anchored at `(2,1)` and `(12,1)` (0-indexed); recolor only those mask cells to 5 and preserve the seed and all other cells. Requiring non-mask cells to be non-background wrongly excludes these validated matches. This signature can recur as a compact colored template with scattered exact mask-color/marker locations.

Validated additional seed-mask rule (task-e6f5b2c7): background 9, template color 4. The 4-mask is the L triomino in a 2x2 bounding box, relative coordinates `{(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)}` (top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right; equivalently all except top-left). In the demo, all-zero matches of this three-cell mask were changed to 4, preserving all other cells, including arbitrary values at the non-mask/top-left position.
